slots.hypothesis: W = (RS+ - RS-)/sum|r|. The information is in how one-sided the day was (its size), not in which way it went: signed W -0.19, W^2 +0.89, W^4 +1.18. But W^2 mixes three things: vol scale sigma^2, jump/kurtosis, and true one-sidedness. The outer pow_2 has the same daily rank as W^2, so it adds nothing on a given day; its +0.29 comes only from the EMA, and it splits train +0.29 / valid -0.31. That is convexity bringing vol back in (traps 1/3). The periphery here (1) removes vol scale nonlinearly: same-day RV denominator, so div(W^2, day_wmean(abs_(Ret),Ret)^2) = RSJ^2 (Bollerslev-Li-Zhao), or a rank inside 20-day vol deciles (cs_bucket_rank); (2) makes the monthly aggregation explicit and separates typical days from tail days (cross_med/mean/tail_mean_q75/quantile_q75/max, 20 days) plus a 'shock vs own history' cross_zscore; (3) normalises by price-limit width (Hung-Yang 2018). There are 13 seeds, all 20-day aggregates or within-decile ranks, so their daily rank correlation with the head and with the controls should be low. Why it should hold out of sample: lottery/attention demand for jumpy one-sided stocks under A-share short-sale limits and price limits (Bali et al. 2011; Nartea et al. 2017: in A-shares MAX and IVOL coexist). Once vol scale and the train-picked convexity are removed, whatever is left is structural.

The size of intraday order-flow imbalance (VPIN-type flow toxicity) from minute bars predicts returns; expected sign is negative. Each minute's turnover is tagged buy or sell by the sign of its return (hard bulk classification). Built at daily level as |day_signed_ratio(Ret, Amt)| and at bucket level as day_mean(|in_sum_rolling(sign(Ret)*Amt, 15/30)| / in_sum_rolling(Amt, 15/30)) (Easley-Lopez de Prado-O'Hara 2012). Aggregated over 20 days, plus a shock z-score against the stock's own 60 days. Further seeds: how unstable the flow direction is (cross_stddev), price impact in the heaviest-turnover minutes (topw_mean/day_std), and flow-price divergence. Three seeds are ranked inside 20-day turnover deciles to remove liquidity nonlinearly. Sign: A-share persistent one-sided flow is attention-driven (Chen et al. 2022, negative) versus the US PIN information-risk premium (Easley-Hvidkjaer-O'Hara 2002, positive); the reward picks the sign on train. Inputs and mechanism both differ from the head. It should hold out of sample because short-sale limits, price limits and the retail share of trading are institutional features of the market; all windows are standard (15/20/30/60). 12 seeds.

The periphery removes the vol scale nonlinearly (the same-day RSJ^2 denominator, or ranks inside vol deciles), makes the 20-day aggregation explicit (typical days vs tail days, plus a cross_zscore shock), and normalises by price-limit width (LimitWidth).
- **Slot b, N**, 12 seeds: size of intraday order-flow imbalance (VPIN-type) from minute bars, at daily level and in 15/30-minute buckets, aggregated monthly. Three seeds are ranked inside turnover deciles to take out liquidity.
- **R**: 11 variants on the head pow_2(pow_2(day_wmean(Ret, Ret))), aimed at three parts:
  - the outer pow_2, which has the same daily rank as W^2 and splits train +0.29 / valid -0.31;
  - the vol scale inside W (trap 3);
  - the |r| self-weighting, which has never been tested.
- I left out the analysis's pure-vol and zero-ratio null variants and a fold-after-mean variant. If any of them beat the head by 0.1 or more, it would enter the library as a trap-exploiting factor.

Before writing I checked that every expression parses. The pipeline's correlation table has not run, so I don't know yet which seeds get struck. Two numbers rest only on my own back-of-envelope estimate:
- The core's daily rank correlation with the vol control should be about 0.3. If it reaches 0.5, the E slot fails no matter what.
- The RSJ^2 seeds may correlate 0.3-0.5 with liquidity or size, so I added seeds ranked within turnover deciles as a hedge.
